Definition: from G5259 and G1166; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish):--show, (fore-)warn.
BiblicalUsage: hypodeíknymi turns up where the Bible says to show, to warn beforehand. In Matthew 3:7, the text says "who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?" In Luke 3:7, the text says "who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?"
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hypodeíknymi this way, I believe God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Baptism of Jesus; The Conversion of Paul; The Sermon on the Mount
